question: What is the primary endpoint of the study?
expected_answer: Clinical and endoscopic remission at Week 12 (full Mayo score ≤2, no individual subscore >1, rectal bleeding subscore = 0); plus adverse events, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, and clinical safety lab abnormalities.

question: What is the investigational medicinal product?
expected_answer: TJ301 (FE 999301, Olamkicept), 15 mg/mL solution for injection.

question: What is the indication for this study?
expected_answer: Active ulcerative colitis.

question: What phase is this trial?
expected_answer: Phase 2.

question: How many patients will be randomised and in what ratio?
expected_answer: 90 patients, 1:1:1, to 600 mg TJ301 Q2W, 300 mg TJ301 Q2W, or placebo Q2W.

question: What is the dosing schedule of the study drug?
expected_answer: 600 mg or 300 mg TJ301 (or placebo) every 2 weeks (Q2W), administered on Days 0, 14, 28, 42, 56, and 70.

question: How is randomisation stratified in this study?
expected_answer: By prior corticosteroids treatment (yes/no) and consent to participate in the PK substudy (yes/no).

question: What is the eligible age range for patients?
expected_answer: 18–70 years of age (inclusive).

question: What are the study periods and their durations?
expected_answer: Run-in period (if needed), 4-week Screening, 12-week Treatment, and 3-week Safety Follow-up to Day 105.

question: How many site visits are there and what are they?
expected_answer: 9–10 main visits: Visit 0 (run-in, optional), Visit 1 (screening), Visit 2 (randomisation/baseline), Visits 3–7 (treatment), Visit 8 (End of Treatment, Week 12), Visit 9 (safety follow-up, Day 105).

question: What is the infusion time for the study drug?
expected_answer: 2 hours.

question: How is the study drug stored and prepared?
expected_answer: Stored at -20±5°C, thawed at site, and diluted in 250 mL 5% (w/v) glucose.

question: What is the planned sample size and statistical power?
expected_answer: N=72 (24 per arm) for 83% power to detect a 30% remission difference (10% placebo vs 40% highest dose), Pearson chi-square, one-sided p<0.05. (90 randomised.)

question: In which countries is the trial being conducted?
expected_answer: Mainland China, Taiwan, Republic of Korea, and Australia.

question: What is the definition of clinical and endoscopic remission?
expected_answer: Full Mayo score ≤2, with no individual subscore >1 and a rectal bleeding subscore = 0.

question: What is the size of the PK subgroup and where is it based?
expected_answer: 24 patients (8 per arm) in Mainland China.

question: What are all the secondary endpoints?
expected_answer: Clinical & endoscopic response (W12); clinical remission (W4–12); clinical response (W4–12); mucosal healing (Mayo endoscopic subscore 0/1 at W12); changes in 9-point partial, full, and modified Mayo scores; PGA changes; FDA-defined remission (W12); immunogenicity (anti-TJ301 antibodies); PK parameters; peak & trough TJ301 concentration.

question: What are the key inclusion criteria?
expected_answer: Age 18–70; active UC confirmed by colonoscopy/sigmoidoscopy with biopsy extending >15 cm past anal verge; full Mayo ≥5 with rectal bleeding subscore ≥1; endoscopy subscore ≥2; on stable conventional non-biologic therapy; contraception; able to complete Patient Diary; signed ICF.

question: What are the main exclusion criteria?
expected_answer: Pregnancy/breastfeeding; allergy to TJ301; colectomy history; Crohn's/other colitis; anaemia (Hb<9)/thrombocytopenia/creatinine>2; autoimmune disease (except Sjögren's/hypothyroidism); C. difficile; chronic liver disease; hepatitis B/C, HIV; active/latent TB; recent live vaccines/IV corticosteroids/immunosuppressants; etc.

question: What exploratory biomarkers are measured in this study?
expected_answer: ESR, C-reactive protein (CRP), IL-6, IL-6/sIL-6R complex, neutrophil and platelet count, and faecal calprotectin.

question: What assessments are performed at the Week 12 (End of Treatment) visit?
expected_answer: Disease activity assessment plus endoscopy (colonoscopy or sigmoidoscopy) with mucosal biopsies for mucosal healing, histology, and immunohistochemistry.

question: How is CRP used for stratification in this study?
expected_answer: TRAP: CRP is NOT a current stratification factor. It is an exploratory biomarker only. Stratification is by prior corticosteroids treatment and PK-substudy consent. CRP-based stratification (≥3 mg/L) was in the SUPERSEDED v1.0. A correct answer gives the current factors and/or labels the CRP version as historical.

question: What are the current randomisation stratification factors?
expected_answer: Prior corticosteroids treatment (yes/no) and consent to participate in the PK substudy (yes/no). Must NOT return the CRP version.

question: What changed in the randomisation stratification between protocol versions?
expected_answer: Changed from 'elevated (≥3 mg/L) CRP levels and stable conventional treatment' (v1.0) to 'prior corticosteroids treatment and PK-substudy consent' (v1.1).

question: Which countries changed between protocol versions?
expected_answer: Germany was removed and Australia added in v1.1.

question: What is the name of the safety committee in the current protocol?
expected_answer: Safety Review Committee (SRC). Renamed from DSMC in v1.1.

question: What does CRP refer to and how is it used in this protocol?
expected_answer: C-Reactive Protein; used as an exploratory biomarker measured at local sites — not a stratification factor in the current protocol.
